chapter: Cincinnati, Buffalo, Russell and Fletcher Henderson
title: Louis Armstrong and leaving his band
summary: Armstrong was the greatest and they were close; he gave notice to manager Joe Garland.

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: Could you explain anything about that time up until - what songs you recorded and anything about Louis Armstrong at that period?
Yes. What you recorded, what the band was like, what was Louis Armstrong like.
The greatest in the world! Greatest, and he'd always see

that I played something, always, because he and I were like this. He would sit here and I would sit here, and Lou and I were like this. We'd get the work, we'd go out, you know, to do one-nighters. He'd say, "Come on now, let's go out and sport a while." We were like that. I didn't even give him two-weeks notice because I was ashamed. I gave it to the manager.
He was the manager of the band? Not Joe Glaser?
So, why did I leave. It took me two days, three days. They wouldn't let me get on a plane.
